The honest lever is `coverage: "PARTIAL"` usage rows, which is what the committed PARTIAL arm already drives; it yields LOWER_BOUND lines and a QUARANTINED (retained, unpruned) settlement.

I READ `coverageOf` RATHER THAN ASSUMING THE BRANCH, as the step demanded (budget-current-projection.ts:164-184). Its order is: UNKNOWN if any line is UNKNOWN_HELD **or openHoldCount > 0**; else PARTIAL if any line is LOWER_BOUND or CONSERVATIVE_WRITE_OFF; else COMPLETE. Two consequences I designed against:
1. `openHoldCount > 0` DOMINATES. So the arm must use the single-activation `activatedStore`, never the two-attempt fixture — a second unsettled reservation on the same meter would drive the read to UNKNOWN and the arm would fail for a reason unrelated to the receipt.
2. `refundable` is non-null only at COMPLETE (:184), which is why asserting NULL separates PARTIAL from COMPLETE instead of restating the enum.

- projection.coverage === "PARTIAL" on the named meter
- projection.buckets.quarantined > 0 and buckets.meter === meter (the conserved position survives; the unmeasured remainder is HELD, which is what makes it a lower bound)
- projection.refundable === null
- GUARD A: the settlement is SERVED, not merely un-refused — the arm throws with the refusal's code@layer if `ok !== true`, so it can never assert reader behaviour on a store where no settlement landed.
- GUARD B: `coverage.ok` is checked before reading `meters`, so a refusal cannot silently produce an undefined projection.
